section_1.title: Software and hardware considerations
section_1.paragraph_1: The CDTT software was developed as a cross-platform Java application and it can be run on different operating systems (e.g., Windows, macOS).
bullet_pts: The main interface provides controls for the test operator to enter participant information, select test parameters, run a test, and save the results in MS-Excel.
Participants enter their digit responses on-screen or using an external USB numeric keypad.
Use of an external USB sound card (e.g., E10K Olympus 2 by FiiO) is recommended for portability and reproducibility across computers.
Results have been found to be largely insensitive to the choice of earphones, but use of Radioear DD45 audiometric earphones is recommended for strict comparison to the

Results obtained to date suggest that hearing screening with the CDTT can be administered with supra-aural earphones (Radioear DD45 or similar) on testing sites with background noise levels not exceeding 60 dBA, while the use of sound-attenuating circumaural earphones (Radioear DD450 or similar) should be considered on testing sites with background noise levels up to 75 dBA.

section_2.title: Software and hardware considerations
bullet_pts: Testing languages: Canadian English and French (2016), Asante-Twi and Ghanaian English (2023)
Talkers: one or two talkers (male and female) per language/dialect
Maskers: Talker-specific speech spectrum noise (default) and user-defined noises
Test modes: Adaptative speech-recognition threshold search (SRT) or fixed signal-to-noise ratio (SNR)
